A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DiGraP research work, with readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. All 21 pages were compared; the appendices are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original DiGraP experiments on image classification, visual question answering, and BOSS sentiment analysis, plus ablations and distribution-shift analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–11 and the main-text and appendix figures.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the unconstrained-update condition from a gradient inner product < 0 to ≥ 0, placing projection in the conflicting-gradient branch. This localized algorithm correction restores agreement with the existing Section 3.2 and Figure 1; it does not establish that the experimental implementation changed.

E1.justification: Sections 4 and 4.3 replace 'OK-VQAv2' with 'OK-VQA'. Tables 3 and 6 and the appendix histograms already identify OK-VQA in v1 and remain unchanged, supporting a naming correction rather than changed dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within every corresponding experiment, including the image-classification, VQA, BOSS, and LP-FT-C controlled comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, backbones, evaluation metrics, training budgets, model-selection procedures, and LoRA configurations are unchanged, including those in Appendices 7.1–7.3.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same fixed-versus-trainable projection ablation, sensitivity sweeps, LP-FT-C control, training-dynamics visualizations, and distribution-shift correlation and histogram analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. No repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance tests are added or removed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–11, plotted results, and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains DiGraP's 87.40 ID accuracy, 63.50 overall OOD average, and 49.20 OK-VQA accuracy.

T1.justification: The objective definitions, projection and hypergradient derivations in Equations 1–8, and Mahalanobis-distance definition in Equation 9 are unchanged. The Algorithm 1 correction implements the already-stated mathematical condition without revising the underlying reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about trainable directional gradient projection, multimodal robust-fine-tuning evaluation, and ID/OOD performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of VQA fine-tuning and WiSE-FT/FTP behavior remain unchanged, as do the limitations concerning far-OOD performance, regularization trade-offs, and untested training from scratch or non-robust initialization.

D1.justification: The training hyperparameters, software, hardware, LoRA details, and model-selection information in Appendix 7.2 are unchanged. Appendix 7.3's feature-extraction instructions and the code-availability link are also retained.

R1.justification: Two dataset citations and the bibliography replace Reichman et al. (2023), Outside Knowledge Visual Question Answering Version 2.0, with Marino et al. (2019), OK-VQA. This is a limited attribution correction; the broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is limited to the dataset name and accompanying citations, plus the arXiv version/date stamp. The narrative, section ordering, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The citation replacement causes minor line wrapping and bibliography reflow, including moving Tian et al. (2023a) from page 13 to page 12. Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–11 retain their content, formatting, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes Algorithm 1's reversed branch condition, resolving a contradiction with Section 3.2 that could lead to an incorrect implementation. It also aligns the dataset name and citation with the existing OK-VQA results. These targeted corrections improve accuracy and reproducibility, while the experimental evidence, analyses, and conclusions remain unchanged.
